data.title: Input
data.tagline: Let the user enter one line of text
data.description: Use a text input for an account name, nickname, search query, or anything else that fits on one line. Give it a label that stays visible after typing. If the value is invalid, explain what is wrong and how to fix it near the field.

distinctions.label: Search input
distinctions.explanation: A search input is an Input with a specific purpose and may include submit, clear, or suggestion behavior. A normal input can collect any short value, such as a name or email.

distinctions.label: Autocomplete
distinctions.explanation: Input accepts text. Autocomplete offers possible matches as someone types.

avoid: Collect a long answer that needs several lines
Use placeholder text as the only label
Wait until final submission to reveal every obvious error
Show read-only content in a field that looks editable

lessonPractice.title: Checkout needs a recipient name. It is usually short and is not chosen from a fixed list. What should the form use?

options.label: A single-line input with a persistent Recipient name label
options.feedback: A name is short free-form text, so a labeled single-line input matches both the value and the task.

options.label: A resizable textarea with room for complete information
options.feedback: A textarea suits comments or descriptions; its extra height adds no useful capability for a name.

options.label: A dropdown containing only a list of preset names
options.feedback: The value must be freely entered, so fixed options would block valid names outside the list.

data.agentPrompt: Add a single-line Recipient name input to checkout and keep its label visible after typing. Test an empty value, a normal name, and a long name, with any error shown beside the field.

references.title: Help users enter data in forms
